name: FirstUK Bank Compliance Training Manual
description: Mandatory compliance training manual for all FirstUK Bank staff covering AML, KYC, fraud, privacy, and incident response. Effective from 2026-01-15 with annual review cycle.

name: Mandatory Annual Compliance Training
description: A mandatory annual training program covering regulatory requirements, customer protection, anti-money laundering, know-your-customer verification, GDPR, fraud prevention, and reporting obligations. This is the overarching training program that encompasses multiple compliance domains.
context: Mandatory annual compliance training covering regulatory requirements, customer protection, anti-money laundering (AML), know-your-customer (KYC), GDPR, fraud prevention, and reporting obligations.

name: Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Module
description: Training module covering anti-money laundering regulatory requirements and compliance obligations as part of the mandatory annual compliance training program.

name: Know-Your-Customer Verification Module
description: Training module covering know-your-customer verification requirements and customer due diligence obligations as part of the mandatory annual compliance training program.

name: GDPR Compliance Module
description: Training module covering General Data Protection Regulation requirements and data protection obligations as part of the mandatory annual compliance training program.

name: Fraud Prevention Module
description: Training module covering fraud prevention, detection, and response procedures as part of the mandatory annual compliance training program.

name: Reporting Obligations Module
description: Training module covering regulatory reporting obligations and suspicious activity reporting requirements as part of the mandatory annual compliance training program.

name: Customer Protection Module
description: Training module covering customer protection requirements and regulatory safeguards as part of the mandatory annual compliance training program.

name: Regulatory Requirements Module
description: Training module covering general regulatory requirements and compliance framework as part of the mandatory annual compliance training program.

name: Module 1 — AML & Sanctions Compliance
description: Mandatory annual training module covering Anti-Money Laundering and Sanctions Compliance requirements for all staff. Module includes assessment with 80% pass threshold and certificate upon completion.
context: Frequency: Annual (or immediately upon change in regulations)
Assessment: Quiz at end of each module (pass = 80%+)

name: Module 2 — Know Your Customer (KYC)
description: Mandatory annual training module on Know Your Customer verification and customer due diligence procedures. Requires 80% pass threshold on end-of-module quiz with certificate issued upon completion.
context: Assessment: Quiz at end of each module (pass = 80%+)

name: Module 3 — GDPR & Data Protection
description: Mandatory annual training module covering GDPR and data protection compliance obligations for all staff. Includes end-of-module assessment with 80% pass threshold and certificate issuance.
context: Assessment: Quiz at end of each module (pass = 80%+)

name: Module 4 — Fraud Prevention
description: Mandatory annual training module on fraud prevention and detection for all staff. Requires passing end-of-module quiz at 80% threshold with certificate issued upon completion.
context: Assessment: Quiz at end of each module (pass = 80%+)

name: Module 5 — Reporting Obligations
description: Mandatory annual training module covering staff reporting obligations and procedures. Includes end-of-module quiz with 80% pass threshold and certificate upon successful completion.
context: Assessment: Quiz at end of each module (pass = 80%+)

name: Module 6 — Consequences of Non-Compliance
description: Mandatory annual training module explaining the consequences and penalties for non-compliance with regulatory and internal requirements. Requires 80% pass threshold on end-of-module quiz with certificate issued upon completion.
context: Assessment: Quiz at end of each module (pass = 80%+)

name: Mandatory Training Completion for All Staff
description: All staff are required to complete the six mandatory compliance training modules annually or immediately upon regulatory change. Completion is tracked and certificated.
context: Frequency: Annual (or immediately upon change in regulations)

name: Module Assessment Pass Threshold
description: Staff must achieve a minimum pass score of 80% on the quiz at the end of each mandatory training module to demonstrate competency and receive the completion certificate.
context: Assessment: Quiz at end of each module (pass = 80%+)

name: Module 1 — AML & Sanctions Compliance
description: A mandatory staff training module covering Anti-Money Laundering (AML) fundamentals, the definition and process of money laundering, regulatory requirements under UK law, and the consequences of non-compliance including FCA fines and criminal prosecution. The module establishes staff responsibility for identifying and reporting suspicious activity.
context: Money laundering is the process of converting illegally obtained money into legitimate-looking funds. AML rules are designed to prevent this.
FirstUK Bank must comply with UK law (Money Laundering Regulations 2017)
Violations result in: FCA fines (>£10M), criminal prosecution, loss of license

name: Understanding Money Laundering Definition and Process
description: Staff must understand what money laundering is and how it operates as the conversion of illegally obtained money into legitimate-looking funds, as foundational knowledge for AML compliance.
context: Money laundering is the process of converting illegally obtained money into legitimate-looking funds.
AML rules are designed to prevent this.

name: Identifying and Reporting Suspicious Activity
description: Staff must develop the capability to identify suspicious activity and understand their role in reporting it as a core AML compliance responsibility.
context: Your role: Identify and report suspicious activity

name: Compliance with UK Money Laundering Regulations 2017
description: FirstUK Bank must comply with the Money Laundering Regulations 2017 as a legal requirement under UK law. Non-compliance carries severe consequences including FCA fines exceeding £10M, criminal prosecution, and loss of banking license.
context: FirstUK Bank must comply with UK law (Money Laundering Regulations 2017)
Violations result in: FCA fines (>£10M), criminal prosecution, loss of license

name: Suspicious Activity Reporting Obligation
description: Staff have a mandatory obligation to identify and report suspicious activity as part of FirstUK Bank's AML compliance framework and regulatory duty.
context: Your role: Identify and report suspicious activity

name: Suspicious Activity Detection and Reporting Process
description: A multi-stage compliance process triggered when suspicious activity is detected on a customer account. The process requires reporting to the internal Compliance Team, conducting an investigation, and escalating to the FCA when necessary, with potential referral to law enforcement.

name: Suspicious Activity Detection
description: The initial trigger point in the AML process where suspicious activity is identified on a customer account, requiring immediate escalation to the Compliance Team for investigation.

name: SAR Filing to FCA
description: The obligation to file a Suspicious Activity Report to the FCA when an investigation determines that suspicious activity meets the threshold for regulatory reporting. Filing occurs conditionally based on investigation findings.

name: Multiple Large Deposits Followed by Immediate Large Withdrawals
description: A transaction pattern where a customer receives multiple large deposits into their account and then immediately withdraws or transfers out large sums. This pattern is indicative of potential money laundering activity, particularly layering or placement stages.
context: Multiple large deposits followed by immediate large withdrawals

name: Frequent Transfers to Multiple Accounts or Jurisdictions
description: A pattern of frequent fund transfers to multiple different accounts and/or transfers to accounts in multiple jurisdictions. This behaviour may indicate an attempt to obscure the origin or destination of funds across borders.

name: Round-Number Transactions
description: Transactions conducted in exact round amounts such as £10,000 or £20,000 rather than natural transaction amounts. This pattern may indicate deliberate structuring to avoid reporting thresholds or to obscure the true nature of fund movements.

name: Transfers to High-Risk Countries
description: Fund transfers directed to countries designated as high-risk for money laundering, terrorism financing, or sanctions concerns. Such transfers require immediate investigation and potential escalation.

name: Transactions Inconsistent with Customer Profile
description: Financial transactions that deviate significantly from the customer's known profile, occupation, income level, or historical transaction behaviour. This inconsistency may indicate account compromise, fraud, or illicit activity.

name: Pensioner Large Transfer to Shell Company in High-Risk Jurisdiction
description: A specific high-risk scenario where a pensioner customer suddenly transfers a large sum (£50,000) to a shell company registered in a high-risk jurisdiction such as Panama. This pattern is highly inconsistent with typical pensioner profiles and suggests potential fraud, elder abuse, or money laundering.
context: A pensioner suddenly transferring £50,000 to a shell company in Panama

name: Reluctance to Provide Documentation
description: A customer exhibits unwillingness or resistance to supplying required identity, address, or beneficial ownership documentation during account opening or ongoing KYC verification. This is a key indicator of potential money laundering or account misuse.

name: Vague Account Purpose Statement
description: A customer is unable or unwilling to clearly articulate the legitimate business or personal purpose for opening or using the account. This vagueness prevents proper risk assessment and source of funds verification.

name: Inconsistent Transaction Purpose Narrative
description: A customer provides conflicting or changing explanations for the purpose or nature of transactions on their account. This inconsistency suggests potential deception or concealment of the true source or use of funds.

name: Third-Party Proxy Use for Account Activity
description: A customer uses another person as an intermediary or proxy to conduct transactions on their account rather than conducting transactions directly themselves. This arrangement may indicate structuring, layering, or an attempt to obscure the beneficial owner.

name: Dormancy Following Large Deposit
description: A customer opens an account, makes a significant deposit, but then fails to use the account for its stated purpose or for normal banking activity. This pattern is consistent with money laundering placement and layering techniques.
context: Avoids using account normally after opening
Customer opens account, deposits £30,000, then has friend withdraw it

name: Large Deposit Followed by Third-Party Withdrawal
description: A customer deposits a substantial sum into a newly opened account and then immediately arranges for a third party to withdraw the funds. This pattern is a classic indicator of money laundering, structuring, or account misuse to obscure beneficial ownership and fund origins.
context: Customer opens account, deposits £30,000, then has friend withdraw it

name: Money Services Business Activity
description: Money services and remittance businesses are identified as high-risk activities requiring enhanced AML scrutiny. Staff must recognize customers or account holders engaged in remittance services as presenting elevated compliance risk.

name: Casino and Gambling Business Activity
description: Casinos and gambling operations are flagged as high-risk business activities due to their cash-intensive nature and potential for money laundering. Staff should apply enhanced due diligence to customers involved in this sector.

name: Art and Jewelry Dealer Business Activity
description: Art dealers and jewelers are classified as high-risk businesses due to the high value and portability of goods, which can facilitate money laundering and asset concealment. Enhanced KYC and transaction monitoring apply.

name: Cash-Intensive Retail Business Activity
description: Cash-intensive retail operations present elevated AML risk due to the difficulty in tracing the source and destination of funds. Staff must apply heightened monitoring to customers engaged in this business type.

name: Used Car Dealership Business Activity
description: Used car dealerships are identified as high-risk businesses, typically involving large cash transactions and high-value asset transfers that can mask money laundering activity. Enhanced due diligence is required.

name: High-Value Goods Trade Business Activity
description: Businesses dealing in high-value portable goods such as watches and handbags are flagged as high-risk due to their susceptibility to money laundering through asset purchases and resale. Enhanced monitoring and KYC procedures apply.

name: OFAC Sanctioned Country Risk
description: Staff must recognise customer or transaction connections to countries on the OFAC sanctions list as a high-risk indicator requiring immediate escalation. The OFAC list includes Iran, North Korea, Syria, Crimea, Cuba, and Sudan.
context: OFAC List: Iran, North Korea, Syria, Crimea, Cuba, Sudan

name: EU Consolidated Sanctions List Entity Risk
description: Staff must identify customers or entities appearing on the EU Consolidated Sanctions List as a compliance red flag requiring verification and potential escalation.
context: EU Consolidated List: Various sanctioned entities

name: HMT UK Sanctions List Entity Risk
description: Staff must screen customers and transactions against the UK Her Majesty's Treasury sanctions list to identify additional UK-sanctioned entities beyond OFAC and EU lists.

name: High-Corruption Country Risk
description: Staff must treat customers with connections to high-corruption countries as elevated risk, requiring enhanced due diligence and source of funds verification. Identified high-corruption countries include Nigeria, Zimbabwe, and Venezuela.

name: Sanctions Screening
description: Mandatory screening process against multiple sanctions lists including OFAC, EU Consolidated List, and HMT UK sanctions to identify and prevent transactions with sanctioned countries and entities.
context: OFAC List: Iran, North Korea, Syria, Crimea, Cuba, Sudan
EU Consolidated List: Various sanctioned entities

name: New Customer Sanctions and PEP Screening
description: Mandatory screening process executed upon account opening for new customers against multiple sanctions lists and PEP databases. Screening must clear before account can be opened, and any matches are escalated immediately to Compliance.
context: Screen against: OFAC, EU Consolidated List, HMT Sanctions, UN Sanctions, PEP Database
Review results (must be clear before account opens)
If match found: Escalate to Compliance immediately

name: New Customer Identity and Address Collection
description: Initial KYC data collection process for new customers at account opening, requiring capture of customer name, date of birth, and address. This information forms the basis for subsequent screening and compliance checks.

name: Screening Result Documentation
description: Mandatory obligation to document all screening results for new customer accounts. This creates an audit trail and evidence of compliance with AML screening requirements.

name: Immediate Escalation of Screening Matches
description: Mandatory obligation to escalate any positive match found during sanctions or PEP screening to the Compliance team immediately. This ensures rapid investigation and appropriate action on potential high-risk customers.
context: If match found: Escalate to Compliance immediately
Screen against: OFAC, EU Consolidated List, HMT Sanctions, UN Sanctions, PEP Database

name: Clear Screening Requirement Before Account Opening
description: Mandatory requirement that screening results must be clear and unambiguous before a new customer account can be opened. This prevents account opening for customers with potential sanctions or PEP matches.
context: Review results (must be clear before account opens)

name: New Customer
description: A customer applying to open an account with the bank, subject to mandatory screening, KYC verification, and compliance checks before account opening is approved.

name: Ongoing Monitoring
description: Monthly AML screening process requiring review of transactions exceeding £5,000, detection of unusual patterns, sanctions list checks, and customer risk assessment. Includes escalation procedures and tipping-off prohibitions.

name: Sanctions List Screening
description: Monthly screening of customer accounts and transactions against updated sanctions lists as part of ongoing AML monitoring obligations.

name: Transaction Processing Suspension on Match
description: Mandatory obligation to suspend transaction processing immediately upon detection of a sanctions list match, pending compliance escalation.
context: If Match Found: Don't process transaction

name: Compliance Escalation on Sanctions Match
description: Mandatory duty to escalate any sanctions list match to the Compliance function immediately upon detection.

name: Tipping-Off Prohibition
description: Strict prohibition against informing customers of sanctions matches or AML investigations, as tipping-off is illegal under AML regulations.
context: Do NOT inform customer (tipping-off is illegal)

name: Unusual Transaction Patterns
description: Detection of unusual patterns in customer transactions during monthly monitoring reviews, requiring investigation and escalation.

name: High-Value Transaction Threshold
description: Transactions exceeding £5,000 are flagged for mandatory review as part of monthly ongoing monitoring procedures.

name: OFAC Sanctions Screening
description: Screening against the US Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctions list covering sanctioned parties from Iran, North Korea, Syria, and other US-designated jurisdictions and entities.
context: OFAC | US-sanctioned parties (Iran, North Korea, Syria, etc.)

name: EU Consolidated Sanctions Screening
description: Screening against the EU Consolidated sanctions list covering EU-sanctioned individuals and entities as designated by European Union authorities.
context: EU Consolidated | EU-sanctioned individuals and entities

name: HMT Sanctions Screening
description: Screening against the UK Home Treasury sanctions list covering parties designated as sanctioned by the United Kingdom authorities.

name: UN Sanctions Screening
description: Screening against United Nations sanctions lists covering individuals and entities designated as sanctioned by UN bodies and member states.
context: UN Sanctions | UN-sanctioned individuals and entities

name: PEP Database Screening
description: Screening against a database of Politically Exposed Persons identified as high-risk individuals due to their political prominence or connections.
context: PEP Database | Politically Exposed Persons (high-risk individuals)

name: Adverse Media Screening
description: Screening to identify individuals who have appeared in news reports or media coverage related to financial crime, money laundering, or other illicit activities.
context: Adverse Media | Individuals in news for financial crime

name: Processing Transaction Despite Potential Match
description: A critical operational error where staff proceed with transaction processing when a potential sanctions or PEP list match has been identified. This represents a failure to escalate and investigate before execution, creating direct compliance and legal risk.
context: Mistake 1: Ignoring a potential match and processing transaction anyway
Correct: Escalate to Compliance, do not process

name: Disclosing Sanctions Screening to Customer
description: A prohibited disclosure where staff inform a customer that they are being checked against sanctions or PEP lists. This constitutes tipping-off, which is illegal under AML regulations and alerts subjects to investigation.
context: Mistake 2: Telling customer 'We're checking if you're on a sanctions list'
Correct: Do not disclose screening to customer (tipping-off is illegal)

name: Account Closure Without Prior Investigation
description: A procedural failure where an account is closed in response to suspicious activity without first reporting to Compliance and conducting investigation. This bypasses mandatory SAR obligations and creates audit and regulatory exposure.
context: Correct: Report suspicious activity to Compliance first

name: One-Time Screening at Account Opening Only
description: A compliance gap where AML screening is performed only at account opening and not repeated throughout the customer relationship. This fails to detect changes in customer risk profile, sanctions list additions, or adverse media developments over time.
context: Mistake 4: Only screening at account opening
Correct: Screen continuously throughout customer relationship

name: Escalation to Compliance on Potential Match
description: Staff must escalate any potential sanctions or PEP list match to Compliance immediately and must not process the transaction pending investigation. This is a mandatory action that takes precedence over transaction processing.
context: Escalate to Compliance, do not process

name: Prohibition on Tipping-Off During Screening
description: Staff must not disclose to customers that they are being screened against sanctions or PEP lists. Tipping-off is illegal under AML law and alerts subjects to investigation, compromising compliance effectiveness.
context: Do not disclose screening to customer (tipping-off is illegal)

name: Mandatory Compliance Reporting Before Account Closure
description: Staff must report suspicious activity to Compliance and conduct investigation before closing an account. Account closure decisions must follow, not precede, compliance review and SAR filing where required.
context: Report suspicious activity to Compliance first

name: Continuous AML Screening Throughout Customer Relationship
description: Staff must perform AML screening not only at account opening but continuously throughout the entire customer relationship. This ongoing monitoring detects changes in risk profile, new sanctions list entries, and adverse media developments.

name: Module 2 — Know Your Customer (KYC)
description: A training module covering the Know Your Customer (KYC) regulatory framework and its core requirements. The module defines the four foundational KYC obligations: collection of customer identity information, verification of customer identity, understanding of customer business and source of funds, and assessment of customer risk level.
context: KYC rules require banks to: 1. Collect customer identity information 2. Verify customer identity 3. Understand customer's business/source of funds 4. Assess customer's risk level

name: Collect Customer Identity Information
description: Staff must understand and be able to execute the requirement to collect customer identity information as part of the KYC process.

name: Verify Customer Identity
description: Staff must be able to verify customer identity through appropriate documentation and processes as mandated by KYC rules.

name: Understand Customer Business and Source of Funds
description: Staff must understand and assess the customer's business activities and the legitimate source of their funds as part of KYC due diligence.

name: Assess Customer Risk Level
description: Staff must be able to evaluate and classify the risk level of a customer based on collected KYC information.

name: Collect Customer Identity Information
description: Banks must collect customer identity information as a mandatory KYC requirement under regulatory rules.
context: KYC rules require banks to: 1. Collect customer identity information

name: Verify Customer Identity
description: Banks must verify customer identity as a mandatory KYC requirement under regulatory rules.
context: KYC rules require banks to: 2. Verify customer identity

name: Understand Customer Business and Source of Funds
description: Banks must understand the customer's business activities and source of funds as a mandatory KYC requirement under regulatory rules.
context: KYC rules require banks to: 3. Understand customer's business/source of funds

name: Assess Customer Risk Level
description: Banks must assess and document the risk level of each customer as a mandatory KYC requirement under regulatory rules.
context: KYC rules require banks to: 4. Assess customer's risk level

name: Primary Identity Document Verification
description: The Know Your Customer process requiring collection and verification of a valid primary identity document. Staff must obtain either a UK Passport or UK Driving License in original form, copy both sides, and perform tampering checks and photo matching as applicable.

name: UK Passport Identity Verification
description: Acceptable primary identity document for KYC verification. The original UK Passport must be valid, both sides must be copied, and the document must be checked for signs of tampering.

name: UK Driving License Identity Verification
description: Acceptable primary identity document for KYC verification. The original UK Driving License must be valid, both sides must be copied, and the photo must be verified to match the customer.

name: Valid Original Document Requirement
description: Mandatory compliance requirement that identity documents must be original and valid. Photocopies alone are not acceptable; staff must see and verify the original document.

name: Document Tampering Check Obligation
description: Mandatory compliance requirement to inspect primary identity documents for signs of tampering or alteration during the KYC verification process.

name: Photo Matching Verification Obligation
description: Mandatory compliance requirement to verify that the photograph on a UK Driving License matches the customer presenting the document.

name: Expired Identity Document
description: Red flag indicating that a presented identity document has expired and is therefore not acceptable for KYC verification purposes. Staff must reject expired documents.

name: Photocopy-Only Identity Document
description: Red flag indicating that only a photocopy of an identity document has been provided without sight of the original. This is not acceptable; staff must insist on viewing the original document.

name: Non-UK Identity Document
description: Red flag indicating that an identity document from a country other than the UK has been presented. Such documents are not acceptable as primary identity verification for this KYC process.

name: Proof of Address Verification
description: The Know Your Customer address verification process requiring customers to provide one of three acceptable document types: utility bill, council tax letter, or bank statement. Each document must meet specific dating and information requirements and must be copied and filed.
context: Must show customer name and address

name: Utility Bill Address Document
description: An acceptable proof of address document in the form of a utility bill. Must be dated within 3 months, show customer name and address, and be copied and filed as part of KYC verification.
context: Must show customer name and address

name: Council Tax Letter Address Document
description: An acceptable proof of address document in the form of a council tax letter. Must be from the current year, show customer name and address, and be copied and filed as part of KYC verification.
context: Must show customer name and address

name: Bank Statement Address Document
description: An acceptable proof of address document in the form of a bank statement. Must be dated within 3 months, show customer name and address, and be copied and filed as part of KYC verification.
context: Must show customer name and address

name: Proof of Address Document Acceptance Requirement
description: The compliance obligation to accept only specific document types as proof of address during KYC verification: utility bills, council tax letters, or bank statements. All other document types including expired documents, P45/P60 tax documents, tenancy agreements, and mobile phone bills must be rejected.
context: Not Acceptable: Expired documents, P45/P60 tax documents, Tenancy agreements, Mobile phone bills

name: Proof of Address Document Dating Requirement
description: The compliance obligation to verify that proof of address documents meet specific dating requirements: utility bills and bank statements must be dated within 3 months; council tax letters must be from the current year.

name: Proof of Address Document Filing Requirement
description: The compliance obligation to copy and file all acceptable proof of address documents as part of the KYC verification process.

name: New Customer Identity and Address Verification
description: A mandatory verification process for every new customer requiring collection and validation of photo ID, proof of address, and confirmation that customer identity matches documentation. The process includes checks for document genuineness, validity, currency, and name/address consistency, with secure filing and system recording of all verification steps.
context: For Every New Customer, verify: Photo ID obtained and genuine
Proof of address dated within 3 months

name: Sanctions List Screening
description: A mandatory AML screening check performed as part of new customer onboarding to verify that the customer does not appear on any sanctions lists. This check is a required component of the verification checklist and must be completed before account opening.

name: Account Opening Verification Documentation Requirement
description: A mandatory obligation to obtain, verify, and securely file copies of all customer identification and address documents, and to maintain a complete system record of all verification checks performed during new customer onboarding.

name: Account Opening Escalation Obligation
description: A mandatory obligation to refuse account opening and escalate to a manager if any verification check fails during the new customer onboarding process.
context: If Any Check Fails: Do not open account. Escalate to manager.

name: New Customer
description: A prospective customer subject to mandatory identity and address verification, sanctions screening, and documentation requirements before account opening can be approved.
context: If Any Check Fails: Do not open account

name: Enhanced Due Diligence
description: A heightened Know Your Customer process applied to higher-risk customer segments including high-net-worth individuals, PEPs, businesses in high-risk industries, and customers in high-risk countries. EDD requires verification of source of funds, collection of business documents, understanding of account purpose, and ongoing monitoring with regular review.
context: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) For Higher-Risk Customers

name: High-Net-Worth Individual
description: A customer with net worth exceeding £500,000, classified as higher-risk and subject to Enhanced Due Diligence procedures including source of funds verification and ongoing monitoring.

name: Politically Exposed Person
description: A customer classified as a Politically Exposed Person, subject to Enhanced Due Diligence requirements including verification of source of funds, business document collection, and ongoing monitoring.

name: Customer in High-Risk Industry
description: A business customer operating in a high-risk industry, subject to Enhanced Due Diligence procedures including verification of source of funds, business document collection, and ongoing monitoring.

name: Customer in High-Risk Country
description: A customer located in or conducting business in a high-risk country, subject to Enhanced Due Diligence procedures including source of funds verification and ongoing monitoring.

name: Source of Funds Verification
description: A mandatory verification step within Enhanced Due Diligence requiring confirmation and documentation of the origin and legitimacy of customer funds.

name: Business Document Collection
description: A mandatory step within Enhanced Due Diligence requiring the collection and review of business documents to verify the legitimacy and nature of the customer's business operations.

name: Account Purpose Understanding
description: A mandatory step within Enhanced Due Diligence requiring staff to understand and document the intended purpose and use of the customer account.

name: Ongoing Monitoring
description: A continuous monitoring requirement for higher-risk customers as part of Enhanced Due Diligence, with regular review of account activity and customer status.

name: Identity Verification
description: The process of verifying a customer's identity by examining original identification documents before account opening. This is a mandatory step that cannot be bypassed regardless of customer relationship or perceived trustworthiness.
context: Opening account without seeing original ID

name: Address Verification
description: The process of verifying a customer's address using current documentation. Address proof must be dated within the last 3 months and cannot be older than this threshold.
context: Accepting address proof dated >3 months ago

name: Universal KYC Application
description: A compliance obligation requiring that Know Your Customer procedures be applied to every customer without exception, regardless of customer relationship status, perceived trustworthiness, or other subjective factors.
context: KYC applies to EVERY customer, no exceptions

name: Documentation-Based Verification Requirement
description: A compliance obligation prohibiting reliance on verbal descriptions or customer statements for verification purposes. All verification must be supported by physical or documented evidence.
context: Relying on verbal description instead of documentation

name: Module 3 — GDPR & Data Protection
description: A training module covering the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and data protection principles. The module introduces GDPR as EU/UK data protection law that regulates how companies collect, use, and store personal data.
context: EU/UK data protection law that regulates how companies collect, use, and store personal data

name: Understanding GDPR Definition and Scope
description: Staff must understand what GDPR is and its scope as EU/UK data protection law governing the collection, use, and storage of personal data by companies.
context: EU/UK data protection law that regulates how companies collect, use, and store personal data

name: Lawfulness of Data Processing
description: A core compliance obligation requiring that all data processing activities must be legal and justified. This principle establishes the foundational requirement that processing must have a lawful basis before any other data protection principles apply.
context: Data processing must be legal and justified
Lawfulness | Data processing must be legal and justified

name: Fairness and Transparency with Customers
description: A compliance obligation requiring staff to be transparent with customers regarding data processing. This principle mandates that customers must be informed about how their data is being used and processed.
context: Fairness | Must be transparent with customers

name: Purpose Limitation
description: A compliance obligation restricting the use of collected data to only the stated and justified purposes. Staff must not repurpose customer data beyond what was originally disclosed and consented to.
context: Only use data for stated purpose
Purpose Limitation | Only use data for stated purpose

name: Data Minimization
description: A compliance obligation requiring that only the minimum necessary data be collected to fulfill the stated purpose. This principle prevents excessive or unnecessary data collection.
context: Data Minimization | Only collect what's needed

name: Data Accuracy
description: A compliance obligation requiring staff to maintain customer data in a current and correct state. This principle establishes the duty to keep records up-to-date and rectify inaccuracies.
context: Accuracy | Keep data current and correct

name: Storage Limitation
description: A compliance obligation restricting the retention period for customer data to only as long as necessary for the stated purpose. This principle requires regular review and deletion of data no longer needed.
context: Only keep data as long as necessary
Storage Limitation | Only keep data as long as necessary

name: Data Integrity and Confidentiality
description: A compliance obligation requiring staff to protect customer data through appropriate security measures. This principle mandates that data must be safeguarded against unauthorized access, loss, or damage.
context: Integrity & Confidentiality | Protect data with security

name: Accountability for Data Processing
description: A compliance obligation requiring staff to document and demonstrate how customer data is processed and protected. This principle establishes the duty to maintain records and evidence of compliance with data protection principles.
context: Document what you do with data
Accountability | Document what you do with data

name: Customer Data Access Request Compliance Obligation
description: Staff must acknowledge customer requests to access personal data and escalate to the Data Protection Officer within the required timeframe. The DPO is responsible for responding with all held data within 30 days of the customer request.
context: I want to see all data you have on me
DPO responds within 30 days with all data

name: Data Protection Officer Escalation Duty
description: All customer data access requests must be escalated to the Data Protection Officer at dpo@firstuk.bank for processing and response. This is a mandatory escalation pathway for subject access requests.
context: DPO responds within 30 days with all data

name: Data Access Response Timeframe Obligation
description: The Data Protection Officer must respond to customer data access requests within 30 days, providing all personal data held by the bank on the requesting customer.
context: DPO responds within 30 days with all data

name: Customer Data Access Request Acknowledgement Obligation
description: Staff must acknowledge receipt of customer data access requests as the first step in the compliance process before escalation to the Data Protection Officer.

name: Customer Requesting Data Access
description: A customer exercising their right to access personal data held by the bank. The customer initiates the request by stating they want to see all data the bank holds on them.
context: I want to see all data you have on me

name: Right to Erasure Request Acknowledgement
description: Staff must acknowledge a customer's right to erasure request when received. This is the first step in the data deletion process and establishes a documented record of the customer's intent.

name: Right to Erasure Escalation to Data Protection Officer
description: Staff must escalate all right to erasure requests to the Data Protection Officer (DPO) for legal review. This ensures compliance with data protection regulations and identifies any legal retention obligations that may override the erasure request.
context: DPO reviews legal requirements (may need to retain for regulatory reasons)

name: Right to Erasure Legal Review and Conditional Deletion
description: The DPO must review legal and regulatory retention requirements before approving data deletion. Data may only be deleted if no legal obligation requires retention. This balances customer privacy rights with regulatory compliance duties.
context: DPO reviews legal requirements (may need to retain for regulatory reasons)

name: Data Protection Officer
description: The Data Protection Officer is the designated authority responsible for reviewing right to erasure requests, assessing legal retention obligations, and determining whether customer data can be lawfully deleted.

name: Right to Portability Request Acknowledgement
description: Staff must acknowledge a customer's request for their data in a portable format and escalate to the Data Protection Officer. This is a mandatory GDPR compliance duty triggered by explicit customer request for data portability.
context: Give me my data in a portable format

name: Data Portability Format Provision
description: The Data Protection Officer must provide customer data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format such as PDF or CSV in response to a portability request. This fulfils the GDPR right to data portability requirement.
context: DPO provides structured, commonly used format (PDF, CSV, etc.)
Give me my data in a portable format

name: Data Portability Request Escalation to DPO
description: All customer requests for data portability must be escalated to the Data Protection Officer for processing and response. This ensures centralised, compliant handling of GDPR data portability rights.
context: DPO provides structured, commonly used format (PDF, CSV, etc.)

name: Customer Requesting Data Portability
description: A customer exercising their GDPR right to data portability by requesting their personal data in a portable, machine-readable format. This customer initiates the portability request process.
context: Customer Request: 'Give me my data in a portable format'

name: Marketing Data Usage Opt-Out
description: A data protection obligation requiring staff to honour customer requests to cease marketing communications. When a customer objects to marketing use of their data, staff must acknowledge the request, stop all marketing communications, document the opt-out in the system, and ensure the preference is respected going forward.
context: Don't use my data for marketing

name: Marketing Communication Cessation
description: The mandatory action to immediately cease all marketing communications to a customer who has exercised their right to object to marketing use of their personal data.
context: Don't use my data for marketing

name: Opt-Out Documentation Requirement
description: The requirement to record and maintain a documented record of the customer's marketing opt-out preference in the bank's system to ensure the preference is tracked and respected in all future interactions.

name: Customer Exercising Right to Object
description: A customer who has exercised their right to object to the use of their personal data for marketing purposes and requires acknowledgment and cessation of marketing communications.
context: Customer Request: 'Don't use my data for marketing'

name: Right to Restrict Processing
description: A customer's right to request that the bank pause data processing during an investigation, except where legal requirements mandate continued processing. Staff must acknowledge the request, implement the processing pause, and resume processing once the investigation concludes.
context: Don't process my data while you investigate

name: Acknowledgment of Data Restriction Request
description: Staff must acknowledge a customer's request to restrict data processing. This is the first required action when a customer invokes their right to restrict processing.

name: Processing Pause During Investigation
description: Staff must pause all data processing activities when a customer requests restriction, with the exception of processing required by law. This pause remains in effect until the investigation is complete.

name: Resume Processing After Investigation
description: Staff must resume normal data processing once the investigation that prompted the restriction request has been completed. This restores the customer's data to active processing status.
context: Your Action: Resume when investigation complete

name: Identity Verification
description: The process of collecting and verifying customer name, date of birth, and address to establish identity for banking services. This is a necessary component of customer onboarding and compliance.

name: Transaction History Monitoring
description: The collection and review of customer transaction history as required for Anti-Money Laundering compliance obligations. This enables detection of suspicious patterns and reporting requirements.

name: Customer Name
description: A template variable representing the customer's full name, collected during identity verification and used across banking communications and account records.

name: Date of Birth
description: A template variable representing the customer's date of birth, collected as part of identity verification requirements for banking services.

name: Customer Address
description: A template variable representing the customer's residential address, collected during identity verification and used for service provision and compliance purposes.

name: Account Information
description: A template variable representing account-level data collected and maintained for service provision to customers.

name: Transaction History
description: A template variable representing historical transaction records collected for AML compliance monitoring and customer account management.

name: Payment Details
description: A template variable representing payment method information collected for transaction processing and service delivery.

name: Contact Preference
description: A template variable capturing the customer's preferred method of contact, with options including email, phone, or SMS. This variable is used to personalise communication delivery in customer-facing templates.

name: Marketing Consent
description: A template variable recording whether a customer has provided separate opt-in consent for marketing communications. This is tracked independently from other consent types to ensure compliance with marketing regulations.

name: Product Preference
description: A template variable capturing customer preferences regarding products and services, used for service improvement and personalisation purposes. This data helps tailor communications and offerings to individual customer needs.

name: Never Collect Without Consent
description: A mandatory compliance obligation prohibiting the collection of sensitive personal data categories without explicit customer consent. The obligation covers political beliefs, religious beliefs, sexual orientation, health information (unless relevant), and criminal records (unless legally required).

name: Prohibition on Collection of Political Beliefs
description: A specific prohibition against collecting data on a customer's political beliefs without explicit consent.

name: Prohibition on Collection of Religious Beliefs
description: A specific prohibition against collecting data on a customer's religious beliefs without explicit consent.

name: Prohibition on Collection of Sexual Orientation
description: A specific prohibition against collecting data on a customer's sexual orientation without explicit consent.

name: Prohibition on Collection of Health Information Without Relevance
description: A specific prohibition against collecting health information unless it is relevant to the banking relationship or service being provided.

name: Prohibition on Collection of Criminal Records Without Legal Requirement
description: A specific prohibition against collecting criminal record data unless legally required by regulatory or statutory obligations.

name: Data Security Compliance Obligation
description: Staff must not share passwords, must log out when leaving their desk, must not discuss customer data publicly, and must lock documents when not in use. These are mandatory data protection duties enforced through employee training and operational procedures.
context: Lock documents when not in use

name: Security Incident Reporting Obligation
description: Staff must report security concerns immediately to appropriate channels. This is a mandatory escalation duty to ensure rapid response to potential data protection breaches or security threats.

name: GDPR Staff Training
description: Mandatory training delivered to all staff on GDPR compliance and data protection principles. The training covers the bank's data security practices and employee responsibilities for protecting customer information.

name: Understanding Data Protection Responsibilities
description: Staff must understand their personal responsibility for protecting customer data, including password security, logout discipline, confidentiality, and document handling. This objective ensures staff recognise data protection as a shared accountability.

name: Recognising and Reporting Security Concerns
description: Staff must be able to identify security concerns and understand the requirement to report them immediately. This objective ensures rapid escalation of potential data protection incidents.

name: Unattended Workstation or Unlocked Documents
description: Staff leaving their desk without logging out or leaving documents unlocked represents a data protection risk and potential unauthorised access to customer information. This is a procedural red flag requiring immediate corrective action.
context: Lock documents when not in use

name: Unauthorised Discussion of Customer Data
description: Staff discussing customer data in public or non-secure settings represents a confidentiality breach and potential GDPR violation. This is a misconduct signal requiring immediate intervention.

name: Data Breach Reporting Obligation
description: Staff must immediately report any discovered data breach to their manager and the Data Protection Officer. The DPO is responsible for notifying the FCA and affected customers within 72 hours of discovery. Attempting to cover up a breach is explicitly prohibited.
context: Do NOT attempt to cover it up
DPO will notify FCA and customers within 72 hours

name: Data Breach Non-Concealment Obligation
description: Staff are explicitly prohibited from attempting to conceal or cover up any data breach. This is a mandatory transparency requirement tied to regulatory and criminal consequences.
context: Do NOT attempt to cover it up

name: Data Breach Access Containment Obligation
description: Upon discovery of a data breach, staff must immediately stop any further unauthorized access to the affected data or systems.

name: Data Breach Discovery
description: The identification or discovery of unauthorized access to customer data or systems constitutes a critical warning sign requiring immediate escalation and containment action.

name: Data Protection Officer
description: The designated Data Protection Officer responsible for receiving breach reports from staff and managing regulatory notifications to the FCA and affected customers within the required 72-hour timeframe.
context: DPO will notify FCA and customers within 72 hours

name: Customer Data Access Request Handling
description: Staff must forward customer data access requests to the Data Protection Officer (DPO) within 24 hours of receipt. This is a mandatory compliance duty under data protection regulations.

name: Third-Party Data Sharing Consent Requirement
description: Staff must obtain explicit customer permission before sharing customer data with any third party, or ensure a legal requirement exists to justify the disclosure.
context: Sharing customer data with third party without consent
Only share with explicit permission or legal requirement

name: Customer Data Retention Period Compliance
description: Staff must delete or archive customer data once the applicable retention period has expired. Keeping data longer than necessary violates data protection obligations.
context: Keeping customer data longer than necessary

name: Confidential Customer Data Privacy in Public Spaces
description: Staff must conduct sensitive conversations involving customer data in private areas to prevent unauthorized disclosure or overhearing by other customers or members of the public.
context: Discussing customer data in public (overhearing customers)
Have sensitive conversations in private area

name: Module 4 — Fraud Prevention
description: A staff training module covering fraud definition, detection systems, staff training responsibilities, customer education, and rapid response protocols at FirstUK Bank. The module establishes foundational knowledge of fraud as deception for financial gain and the bank's multi-layered fraud combat approach.
context: Fraud is deception for financial gain.
At FirstUK Bank, we combat fraud through: Detection systems, Staff training, Customer education, Rapid response

name: Understanding Fraud Definition and Bank's Fraud Combat Approach
description: Staff must understand that fraud is deception for financial gain and recognize FirstUK Bank's multi-layered fraud prevention strategy encompassing detection systems, staff training, customer education, and rapid response mechanisms.
context: Fraud is deception for financial gain.
At FirstUK Bank, we combat fraud through: Detection systems, Staff training, Customer education, Rapid response

name: Fraud Detection and Response Obligation
description: Staff must participate in and support FirstUK Bank's fraud prevention framework, which includes detection systems, training participation, customer education delivery, and rapid response to fraud incidents.
context: At FirstUK Bank, we combat fraud through: Detection systems, Staff training, Customer education, Rapid response

name: Unusual Transactions
description: A red flag indicating suspicious account activity that may signal account takeover or unauthorized access. Staff should recognize unusual transactions as a key indicator requiring investigation and potential escalation.
context: Signs: Unusual transactions, login from new device, password change

name: Login from New Device
description: A warning sign that a customer account may be compromised, indicated by authentication attempts from previously unseen devices. This is a key indicator of potential account takeover requiring monitoring and verification.
context: Signs: Unusual transactions, login from new device, password change

name: Unauthorized Password Change
description: A suspicious indicator that a customer's account credentials have been altered without authorization, potentially signaling account compromise. Staff must recognize this as a critical red flag for account takeover.
context: Signs: Unusual transactions, login from new device, password change

name: Account Takeover
description: A fraud scenario where a fraudster gains unauthorized access to a customer's account. This represents a critical security threat requiring immediate detection, investigation, and customer notification.
context: What It Is: Fraudster gains access to customer's account

name: Two-Factor Authentication Implementation
description: A required security control to prevent account takeover by requiring customers to verify identity through multiple authentication methods. This is a key prevention measure against fraudulent account access.

name: Strong Password Requirement
description: A security requirement that customers maintain strong passwords to protect account access and prevent unauthorized takeover. This is a foundational prevention measure against account compromise.

name: Account Monitoring for Fraud Detection
description: An ongoing obligation to monitor customer accounts for signs of fraud, including unusual transactions and unauthorized access attempts. This continuous surveillance is essential for early detection and prevention of account takeover.

name: Fraudster Impersonation of Customer or Staff
description: A fraud scenario where a fraudster pretends to be either the customer or FirstUK staff member. This is identified when a customer claims they did not authorize a transaction or action. Staff must verify identity and document all authorization to prevent this type of fraud.
context: Fraudster pretends to be customer or FirstUK staff

name: Identity Verification and Authorization Documentation
description: Staff must verify the identity of parties involved in transactions and document all authorizations to prevent impersonation fraud. This is a mandatory control when a customer disputes a transaction or authorization.

name: Large Transaction Without Authorization
description: A transaction of significant monetary value executed on a customer's card or account without the customer's permission or knowledge. This is a key fraud indicator that staff must recognize and escalate.
context: Fraudster uses customer's card/account without permission
Large transaction, unusual merchant, foreign location

name: Transaction at Unusual Merchant
description: A transaction posted to a merchant category or vendor type that is inconsistent with the customer's known spending patterns or account profile. This deviation may indicate unauthorized account use.
context: Fraudster uses customer's card/account without permission
Large transaction, unusual merchant, foreign location

name: Transaction at Foreign Location
description: A transaction processed in a geographic location outside the customer's known residence or typical travel patterns. This geographic anomaly is a red flag for potential card or account compromise.
context: Fraudster uses customer's card/account without permission
Large transaction, unusual merchant, foreign location

name: Unauthorized Card or Account Transaction
description: A fraudulent transaction event in which a fraudster uses a customer's card or account without permission. Detection and response to such events is a core fraud prevention control.
context: Fraudster uses customer's card/account without permission
What It Is: Fraudster uses customer's card/account without permission

name: Fraud Detection Obligation
description: The bank's obligation to implement and maintain fraud detection systems and processes to identify unauthorized transactions on customer cards and accounts. This is a core preventive control.
context: Prevention: Fraud detection, customer education, monitoring

name: Customer Education on Fraud Prevention
description: The bank's obligation to educate customers about fraud risks, unauthorized transaction indicators, and protective measures they should take to safeguard their cards and accounts.
context: Prevention: Fraud detection, customer education, monitoring

name: Transaction Monitoring for Fraud
description: The bank's obligation to continuously monitor customer transactions for signs of fraud, including large amounts, unusual merchants, and foreign locations, and to take appropriate action when suspicious activity is detected.
context: Prevention: Fraud detection, customer education, monitoring

name: Unusual Account Access by Staff Member
description: A red flag indicating that a staff member is accessing customer accounts in an unusual or suspicious manner, potentially indicative of insider fraud. This warning sign requires investigation and escalation through appropriate channels.
context: Staff member uses position to commit fraud
Signs: Unusual account access, undocumented transactions, authority abuse

name: Undocumented Transactions on Customer Account
description: A red flag indicating transactions that lack proper documentation or audit trail, potentially indicating insider fraud or unauthorized account activity. Staff must investigate and document all such occurrences.
context: Signs: Unusual account access, undocumented transactions, authority abuse

name: Abuse of Staff Authority Over Customer Accounts
description: A red flag indicating that a staff member is misusing their position or authority to access, modify, or transact on customer accounts beyond their legitimate business purpose. This is a key indicator of insider fraud.
context: Signs: Unusual account access, undocumented transactions, authority abuse

name: Implement Access Controls for Staff Account Access
description: A compliance requirement to establish and maintain access controls that restrict staff members' ability to access customer accounts, limiting access to only those accounts and functions necessary for their role.
context: Prevention: Access controls, audit logs, whistleblower reporting

name: Maintain Audit Logs of Staff Account Access
description: A compliance requirement to maintain comprehensive audit logs documenting all staff access to customer accounts and transactions, enabling detection and investigation of suspicious activity.
context: Prevention: Access controls, audit logs, whistleblower reporting

name: Establish Whistleblower Reporting Mechanism for Insider Fraud
description: A compliance requirement to establish and maintain a whistleblower reporting mechanism that enables staff and customers to report suspected insider fraud and misconduct without fear of retaliation.
context: Prevention: Access controls, audit logs, whistleblower reporting

name: Customer Appears Coached or Nervous During Interaction
description: A behavioral red flag indicating a customer may be acting under external pressure or instruction during a banking interaction. This sign suggests potential money laundering, fraud, or account takeover activity where the customer is not acting of their own volition.

name: Customer Unable to Explain Transaction Purpose
description: A red flag indicating a customer cannot or will not articulate a legitimate business or personal reason for a transaction. This suggests potential money laundering, structuring, or other illicit activity.

name: Customer Uses Unusual Channels or Transaction Amounts
description: A red flag when a customer deviates from their established banking patterns by using unexpected payment methods or transaction sizes. This may indicate structuring, layering, or other suspicious financial activity.

name: Third Party Present and Controlling Customer Conversation
description: A red flag when a third party is physically present during a customer interaction and appears to be directing or controlling the customer's statements and decisions. This suggests potential fraud, coercion, or money laundering.
context: Third party is present and controlling conversation

name: Customer Requests Immediate Cash Withdrawal After Deposit
description: A red flag indicating a customer deposits funds and immediately requests cash withdrawal, suggesting potential money laundering, structuring, or layering activity. This pattern is commonly used to obscure the source or destination of illicit funds.

name: Teller Colleague Bypasses Internal Controls
description: A red flag indicating a colleague is deliberately circumventing established internal controls or procedures. This suggests potential fraud, collusion, or unauthorized activity.

name: Teller Colleague Works Unusual Hours Alone
description: A red flag indicating a colleague is working outside normal business hours without supervision or oversight. This creates opportunity for unauthorized transactions, fraud, or other misconduct.

name: Teller Colleague Has Unauthorized System Access
description: A red flag indicating a colleague has access to systems, accounts, or functions beyond what their role requires. This creates risk of unauthorized transactions, data theft, or fraud.

name: Teller Colleague Makes Undocumented Exceptions
description: A red flag indicating a colleague is processing transactions or making decisions outside normal procedures without creating an audit trail or documentation. This suggests potential fraud, collusion, or deliberate concealment.

name: Your Role in Fraud Prevention
description: A training module that equips staff to recognize and respond to fraud by monitoring suspicious transactions, questioning anomalies, and reporting concerns. The module emphasizes intuition-based detection and escalation as core fraud prevention responsibilities.
context: Ask questions if something seems off

name: Monitor for Suspicious Transactions
description: Staff must develop the ability to identify and flag transactions that deviate from normal patterns or exhibit characteristics associated with fraud.

name: Recognize Anomalies and Question Irregularities
description: Staff must learn to question transactions or customer behaviour that seems unusual or inconsistent, rather than processing them without scrutiny.
context: Ask questions if something seems off

name: Apply Intuition-Based Fraud Detection
description: Staff are trained to trust their instincts and professional judgment when assessing whether a transaction or customer interaction presents fraud risk.

name: Report Fraud Concerns
description: Staff must understand the obligation and process to escalate suspected fraud to the appropriate authority or team.

name: Obligation to Report Fraud Concerns
description: Staff have a mandatory duty to report any concerns or suspicions of fraud to the appropriate internal or external authority.

name: Suspicious Transaction Pattern
description: Any transaction that deviates from expected customer behaviour or exhibits characteristics inconsistent with the customer's profile warrants investigation and escalation.
context: Ask questions if something seems off

name: Confronting Fraudster
description: A prohibited action that staff must avoid when suspecting fraud. Confronting a suspected fraudster is explicitly flagged as dangerous and counterproductive to fraud investigation.

name: Document Fraud Observations
description: Staff must document all observations related to suspected fraud as part of the escalation and investigation process.

name: Report Fraud to Manager
description: Staff must report suspected fraud to their manager as part of the escalation chain.

name: Report Fraud to Compliance and Financial Crime Team
description: Staff must escalate fraud suspicions to the Compliance and Financial Crime team for formal investigation and potential regulatory reporting.

name: Follow Fraud Policy Procedures
description: Staff must adhere to the established fraud policy procedures when handling suspected fraud cases.

name: Know Your Customer and Anti-Money Laundering Procedures
description: Staff must follow established KYC/AML procedures as part of fraud prevention protocols. This is a foundational compliance duty to prevent fraudulent activity and money laundering.

name: Secure Password Usage
description: Staff must use secure passwords as a fraud prevention measure. This is a security control to protect account access and prevent unauthorized activity.

name: Computer Locking
description: Staff must lock their computers when not in use as a fraud prevention control. This prevents unauthorized access to banking systems and customer data.

name: Credential Non-Disclosure
description: Staff must not share their credentials with any other person. This is a critical security obligation to prevent unauthorized access and fraud.

name: Account Monitoring
description: Staff must monitor their own accounts as part of fraud prevention awareness. This enables early detection of suspicious activity on personal accounts.

name: Help Customers Prevent Fraud
description: A staff training module focused on equipping customers with knowledge and practices to prevent fraud. The module covers security education, transaction monitoring, phishing awareness, and card security practices.

name: Educate Customers on Security Best Practices
description: Staff must be able to educate customers on security fundamentals including strong password creation and two-factor authentication implementation.

name: Encourage Customer Transaction Monitoring
description: Staff must be able to encourage customers to actively monitor their transactions as a fraud prevention measure.

name: Advise Customers on Phishing Scams
description: Staff must be able to advise customers on recognising and avoiding phishing scams and social engineering attempts.

name: Promote Card Security Practices
description: Staff must be able to promote and explain card security practices to customers to prevent card fraud and unauthorised use.

name: Weak or Reused Passwords
description: A security vulnerability that staff should identify when customers use weak or reused passwords, indicating elevated fraud risk.

name: Disabled Two-Factor Authentication
description: A security red flag when customers have not enabled or have disabled two-factor authentication on their accounts.

name: Phishing Attempt
description: A social engineering attack where fraudsters attempt to deceive customers into revealing sensitive information through deceptive communications.

name: Educate Customers on Security Practices
description: Staff must proactively educate customers on security best practices including strong passwords and two-factor authentication to reduce fraud risk.

name: Encourage Active Transaction Monitoring
description: Staff must encourage customers to regularly monitor their account transactions as part of fraud prevention obligations.

name: Advise on Phishing and Social Engineering Risks
description: Staff must advise customers on phishing scams and how to recognise and avoid social engineering attempts.

name: Promote Card Security Practices
description: Staff must actively promote card security practices to customers to prevent card fraud and unauthorised transactions.

name: Direct Debit Guarantee
description: A customer protection scheme that provides automatic refunds for unauthorized Direct Debits, wrong amounts charged, or duplicate payments within 10 days. Customers receive refunds with no questions asked and incur no liability.
context: Unauthorized Direct Debits: Full refund within 10 days
Wrong amount charged: Refund within 10 days

name: Unauthorized Direct Debit Refund Obligation
description: The bank must provide a full refund to customers for unauthorized Direct Debits within 10 days of discovery or claim. This is a mandatory protection with no questions asked.
context: Unauthorized Direct Debits: Full refund within 10 days

name: Wrong Amount Direct Debit Refund Obligation
description: The bank must refund customers within 10 days when an incorrect amount has been charged via Direct Debit.
context: Wrong amount charged: Refund within 10 days

name: Duplicate Payment Refund Obligation
description: The bank must refund customers within 10 days when duplicate Direct Debit payments have been processed.

name: Unauthorized Direct Debit Fraud Event
description: A fraud scenario where a Direct Debit is processed without customer authorization, triggering an automatic refund obligation within 10 days with no liability to the customer.
context: Unauthorized Direct Debits: Full refund within 10 days

name: Unauthorized Card Transaction Chargeback
description: A fraud alert and chargeback process triggered when a customer reports an unauthorized card transaction. The bank disputes the transaction with the card scheme and investigates, with refund issued if the claim is upheld within a typical 3–6 month resolution window.
context: Unauthorized card transactions: Dispute with card scheme
Bank investigates and disputes with merchant

name: Merchant Error Chargeback
description: A chargeback process initiated when a customer disputes a transaction due to merchant error. The bank disputes the transaction with the card scheme to resolve the discrepancy.
context: Merchant error: Dispute with card scheme
Bank investigates and disputes with merchant

name: Item Not Received Chargeback
description: A chargeback process for transactions where the customer reports that an item was not received. The bank disputes the transaction with both the merchant and card scheme to recover funds.
context: Item not received: Dispute with merchant/scheme
Bank investigates and disputes with merchant

name: Fraud Reporting Obligation
description: A mandatory compliance requirement for customers to report card fraud to the bank within 120 days of discovering the unauthorized transaction. Failure to report within this timeframe may affect the customer's eligibility for chargeback protection.

name: Debit Card
description: A payment card subject to chargeback protection and fraud dispute procedures. The card is the instrument through which unauthorized transactions, merchant errors, and item-not-received disputes may occur.
context: Unauthorized card transactions: Dispute with card scheme
Merchant error: Dispute with card scheme
Item not received: Dispute with merchant/scheme

name: Unauthorized Transaction Liability
description: FirstUK Bank's liability framework for unauthorized transactions reported within 120 days, conditional on customer following reasonable security measures, with liability capped at account balance.
context: FirstUK Bank is liable for: Unauthorized transactions you report within 120 days
If you followed reasonable security measures

name: Customer Security Responsibility
description: Customers must follow reasonable security measures to maintain FirstUK Bank's liability protection for unauthorized transactions. Failure to do so, such as sharing passwords or writing down PINs, constitutes gross negligence.
context: If you followed reasonable security measures

name: Fraud Reporting Obligation
description: Customers must report fraudulent transactions within 120 days to maintain FirstUK Bank's liability. Failure to report fraud within this timeframe results in loss of bank liability protection.
context: Fraud you failed to report for >120 days
Unauthorized transactions you report within 120 days

name: Authorized Transaction Non-Liability
description: FirstUK Bank is not liable for transactions that customers have authorized, regardless of whether the customer later regrets the transaction.
context: FirstUK Bank is NOT liable for: Transactions you authorized (even if regretted)

name: Unauthorized Transaction within 120 Days
description: Unauthorized transactions that are reported to FirstUK Bank within 120 days trigger the bank's liability obligation, provided the customer has followed reasonable security measures.
context: Unauthorized transactions you report within 120 days
FirstUK Bank is liable for: Unauthorized transactions you report within 120 days

name: Unreported Fraud Beyond 120 Days
description: Fraudulent transactions that are not reported within 120 days result in FirstUK Bank disclaiming liability, shifting responsibility to the customer.
context: Fraud you failed to report for >120 days
FirstUK Bank is NOT liable for: Fraud you failed to report for >120 days

name: Shared Password or Written PIN
description: Sharing passwords or writing down PINs constitutes gross negligence and disqualifies customers from FirstUK Bank's unauthorized transaction liability protection.
context: FirstUK Bank is NOT liable for: Gross negligence (shared password, written PIN)

name: Fraudster Identification and Vigilance
description: Staff must remain alert to the fact that fraudsters can be very convincing and should not assume fraud is obvious. This obligation emphasizes the need for continuous vigilance and skepticism when evaluating customer interactions and transactions.
context: Fraudsters can be very convincing; stay alert

name: Suspicious Activity Reporting to Compliance
description: Staff must report all concerns and suspicious activity to the Compliance department without exception. This is a mandatory reporting duty that applies to any potential fraud or compliance concern identified.

name: Customer Fraud Report Handling
description: Staff must take all fraud reports from customers seriously and treat them with appropriate urgency and care. This obligation prohibits dismissing or deprioritizing customer-reported fraud concerns.

name: Access Credentials Confidentiality
description: Staff must keep access credentials private at all times and must not share them with any other person or system. This is a fundamental security and data protection obligation.

name: Module 5 — Reporting Obligations
description: A training module covering the types of reports staff must file, with specific focus on Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs). The module defines when SARs must be filed, the procedural steps for filing, and includes a practical example of a suspicious transaction pattern requiring SAR filing.

name: Identify Suspicious Transaction Triggers for SAR Filing
description: Staff must be able to recognise when a transaction or pattern of activity meets the threshold for filing a Suspicious Activity Report, including transactions over £5,000, unusual activity patterns, potential money laundering, fraud indicators, and sanctions list matches.

name: Execute SAR Filing Procedure
description: Staff must be able to follow the complete SAR filing workflow: documenting suspicious activity, reporting to the Compliance Manager, completing the SAR form, submitting to the FCA within the required timeframe, and maintaining documentation of the filing.

name: File SAR for Suspicious Transactions Over £5,000
description: Staff must file a Suspicious Activity Report when a transaction exceeds £5,000 and exhibits suspicious characteristics. This is a mandatory reporting duty triggered by transaction value and suspicious indicators.

name: Report Patterns of Unusual Activity to Compliance Manager
description: Staff must escalate patterns of unusual activity to the Compliance Manager as part of the SAR filing process. This is a mandatory escalation duty that precedes formal SAR submission.

name: Submit SAR to FCA Within 30 Days
description: Staff must submit completed Suspicious Activity Reports to the FCA within 30 days of identifying the suspicious activity. This is a time-bound regulatory reporting obligation.

name: Large Cash Deposit Followed by Immediate Withdrawal to Unknown Party
description: A suspicious pattern where a customer deposits a large sum in cash and immediately withdraws the same amount to an unknown third party. This is a classic money laundering indicator requiring SAR filing. The example provided is a £30,000 deposit followed by £30,000 withdrawal.
context: Customer deposits £30k cash, withdraws £30k to unknown party next day → File SAR

name: Potential Money Laundering Activity
description: A general warning sign indicating indicators of money laundering that trigger SAR filing obligations. Staff must recognise this category of suspicious activity and escalate appropriately.

name: Fraud Indicators in Customer Activity
description: Red flags indicating potential fraud in customer transactions or account activity that meet the threshold for SAR filing. Staff must identify and report these indicators.

name: Sanctions List Match
description: A critical warning sign indicating that a customer or transaction matches a sanctions list, triggering immediate SAR filing obligations and regulatory reporting requirements.

name: Suspicious Activity Report Filing Obligation
description: The mandatory obligation to file a Suspicious Activity Report with the FCA when suspicious transactions or patterns are identified. The filing process includes documentation, Compliance Manager notification, form completion, and submission within 30 days.
