name: Currency Transaction Report Filing Obligation
description: Mandatory obligation to file a Currency Transaction Report with the FCA for any cash transaction exceeding £10,000. Reports must be submitted within 5 business days and include customer identification, transaction details, and purpose information.
context: Whether customer is new or existing

name: Customer Name and ID
description: Customer identification data required in Currency Transaction Reports, including the customer's full name and unique identifier.

name: Transaction Date and Amount
description: The date on which the transaction occurred and the monetary amount involved, required fields in Currency Transaction Reports.

name: Transaction Purpose
description: The stated or known purpose of the cash transaction, reported where available in Currency Transaction Reports.

name: Customer Status
description: Classification indicating whether the customer is new or existing, required in Currency Transaction Reports.
context: Whether customer is new or existing

name: Large Cash Withdrawal Transaction Example
description: Example transaction cited in CTR guidance: a customer withdrawal of £15,000 in cash, which triggers the mandatory Currency Transaction Report filing requirement.
context: Customer withdraws £15,000 in cash → File CTR

name: Counterparty Transaction Report
description: A mandatory reporting obligation requiring staff to file a Counterparty Transaction Report when transactions involve high-risk countries, PEPs, sanctioned parties, or wire transfers outside the UK. The report must include customer details, counterparty details, transaction details, and risk assessment.
context: Transaction with PEP or sanctioned party

name: Transaction Involving High-Risk Countries
description: A red flag indicator that triggers the requirement to file a Counterparty Transaction Report. Transactions with high-risk countries are identified as requiring enhanced scrutiny and reporting.

name: Transaction with PEP or Sanctioned Party
description: A red flag indicator requiring immediate reporting via Counterparty Transaction Report when a transaction involves a Politically Exposed Person or a sanctioned party. This signals elevated AML and sanctions compliance risk.
context: Transaction with PEP or sanctioned party

name: Wire Transfer Outside UK
description: A red flag indicator that triggers the requirement to file a Counterparty Transaction Report. Wire transfers outside the UK are flagged as requiring enhanced monitoring and reporting.

name: Customer Details
description: A required data field in the Counterparty Transaction Report containing information about the customer initiating or involved in the transaction.

name: Counterparty Details
description: A required data field in the Counterparty Transaction Report containing information about the counterparty to the transaction.

name: Transaction Details
description: A required data field in the Counterparty Transaction Report containing information about the transaction itself, including amount, date, and nature of the transaction.

name: Risk Assessment
description: A required data field in the Counterparty Transaction Report documenting the staff member's assessment of the risk level and rationale for filing the report.

name: Whistleblower Report Obligation
description: Staff obligation to report suspected fraud, policy violations, compliance breaches, and misconduct through designated internal, confidential, or external channels. The obligation is protected by law with guaranteed confidentiality and investigation.

name: Internal Whistleblower Reporting Channel
description: Staff must report suspected misconduct internally by speaking to their manager or HR department as the first escalation path for whistleblower concerns.
context: Internal: Speak to manager or HR

name: Confidential Whistleblower Reporting Channel
description: Staff may report suspected misconduct confidentially to the Data Protection Officer at dpo@firstuk.bank for sensitive or internal compliance concerns requiring confidential handling.
context: Confidential: Speak to Data Protection Officer (dpo@firstuk.bank)

name: External Whistleblower Reporting Channel
description: Staff may report suspected misconduct externally to the FCA Whistleblowing service at 0300 500 0023 when internal channels are unavailable or inappropriate.

name: Whistleblower Protection and Confidentiality
description: Legal protection for whistleblowers prohibiting retaliation, maintaining confidentiality of reports, and ensuring investigation is conducted fairly. This is a mandatory protection obligation under whistleblower law.

name: Suspected Colleague Fraud
description: A red flag indicator that staff must recognize and report when they suspect fraudulent activity by a colleague, triggering the whistleblower reporting obligation.

name: Policy Violation Observation
description: A red flag indicator that staff must recognize and report when they observe colleagues violating established policies, triggering the whistleblower reporting obligation.

name: Compliance Breach Observation
description: A red flag indicator that staff must recognize and report when they witness compliance breaches or regulatory violations, triggering the whistleblower reporting obligation.

name: Workplace Misconduct Observation
description: A red flag indicator that staff must recognize and report when they witness general workplace misconduct, triggering the whistleblower reporting obligation.

name: Documentation and Record Keeping Obligation
description: Staff must document and retain records of suspected violations, including date, time, location, people involved, activity details, reason for suspicion, actions taken, and outcome. Records must be stored securely with encryption and limited access.

name: Customer File Retention Obligation
description: Customer files must be retained for 6 years after account closure as a compliance and audit requirement.

name: Transaction Record Retention Obligation
description: Transaction records must be retained for 6 years to support audit, compliance, and dispute resolution requirements.

name: KYC/AML Record Retention Obligation
description: Know Your Customer and Anti-Money Laundering records must be retained for 5–6 years to satisfy regulatory requirements.

name: Suspicious Activity Report Retention Obligation
description: Suspicious activity reports must be retained for a minimum of 5 years to support regulatory oversight and audit trails.

name: Secure Record Storage Obligation
description: Records must be stored securely in locked cabinets, with digital records encrypted, access limited to authorized staff only, and regular backups maintained.

name: Module 6 — Consequences of Non-Compliance
description: A training module that educates staff on the regulatory, financial, and reputational consequences of failing to comply with AML, GDPR, and customer protection obligations. The module covers FCA fines, regulatory enforcement actions, and real-world examples of major penalties imposed on financial institutions.
context: What Happens If You Don't Comply?
AML violations: Up to £10M+ per incident
Recent example: HSBC fined £1.9B for AML failures

name: Understanding FCA Fine Thresholds for AML Violations
description: Staff must understand the financial penalties imposed by the FCA for AML compliance failures, including the scale of fines (up to £10M+ per incident) and real-world enforcement examples.
context: AML violations: Up to £10M+ per incident
Recent example: HSBC fined £1.9B for AML failures

name: Understanding GDPR Breach Penalties
description: Staff must understand the financial penalties imposed for GDPR data protection breaches, including the maximum fine of up to €20M or 4% of annual revenue.
context: GDPR breaches: Up to €20M or 4% revenue

name: Understanding Customer Protection Failure Penalties
description: Staff must understand the financial penalties imposed for customer protection failures, including fines up to £50M+.

name: Recognising Regulatory Enforcement Actions
description: Staff must understand the range of regulatory enforcement actions that can follow non-compliance, including enforcement investigations, asset freezes, license suspension, and in extreme cases, loss of banking license.

name: Understanding Reputational Damage from Non-Compliance
description: Staff must understand the broader reputational and business consequences of non-compliance, including media coverage, customer loss, investor confidence decline, and business disruption.

name: AML Compliance Obligation
description: FirstUK Bank staff must comply with AML regulations to avoid FCA fines of up to £10M+ per incident and regulatory enforcement action including asset freezes and license suspension.
context: AML violations: Up to £10M+ per incident

name: GDPR Data Protection Compliance Obligation
description: FirstUK Bank staff must comply with GDPR requirements to avoid fines of up to €20M or 4% of annual revenue and regulatory enforcement action.
context: GDPR breaches: Up to €20M or 4% revenue

name: Customer Protection Compliance Obligation
description: FirstUK Bank staff must maintain customer protection standards to avoid FCA fines of up to £50M+ and regulatory enforcement action.

name: Module on Criminal Liability and Professional Consequences for Staff
description: A training module addressing the criminal, professional, and financial consequences that staff members face for money laundering facilitation, fraud, data protection breaches, and tipping-off. The module outlines prison sentences, dismissal, industry bans, and financial penalties to reinforce compliance obligations.
context: Money laundering facilitation: Up to 14 years prison
Tipping-off (warning customer of screening): Criminal offense
Industry ban (you can't work in banking)

name: Understanding Criminal Liability for Money Laundering Facilitation
description: Staff must understand that facilitating money laundering carries a criminal penalty of up to 14 years imprisonment, establishing the severity of this compliance obligation.
context: Money laundering facilitation: Up to 14 years prison

name: Understanding Criminal Liability for Fraud
description: Staff must understand that committing or facilitating fraud carries a criminal penalty of up to 10 years imprisonment.

name: Understanding Criminal Liability for Data Protection Breach
description: Staff must understand that data protection breaches carry a criminal penalty of up to 2 years imprisonment.
context: Data protection breach: Up to 2 years prison

name: Understanding the Prohibition on Tipping-Off
description: Staff must understand that warning a customer of AML screening or suspicious activity reporting is a criminal offense and is strictly prohibited.
context: Tipping-off (warning customer of screening): Criminal offense

name: Understanding Professional Consequences of Non-Compliance
description: Staff must understand the professional consequences of compliance failures, including dismissal from FirstUK Bank, industry bans, revocation of professional certification, and employment difficulties.
context: Industry ban (you can't work in banking)

name: Understanding Financial Consequences of Non-Compliance
description: Staff must understand the financial consequences of compliance failures, including criminal fines, civil penalties, compensation to victims, and legal costs.

name: Prohibition on Tipping-Off Customers of AML Screening
description: Staff must not warn or inform customers that they are subject to AML screening, sanctions checks, or suspicious activity reporting. Tipping-off is a criminal offense under AML legislation.
context: Tipping-off (warning customer of screening): Criminal offense

name: Obligation to Comply with Money Laundering Prevention
description: Staff must actively prevent and not facilitate money laundering. Failure to comply carries criminal liability of up to 14 years imprisonment.
context: Money laundering facilitation: Up to 14 years prison

name: Obligation to Comply with Fraud Prevention
description: Staff must not commit or facilitate fraud. Failure to comply carries criminal liability of up to 10 years imprisonment.

name: Obligation to Protect Customer Data
description: Staff must protect customer data and comply with data protection regulations. Breaches carry criminal liability of up to 2 years imprisonment.
context: Data protection breach: Up to 2 years prison

name: Staff Member
description: The staff member or employee of FirstUK Bank who is the subject of this consequences training. The module addresses the criminal, professional, and financial liabilities that apply to staff who fail to comply with AML, fraud prevention, and data protection obligations.
context: Industry ban (you can't work in banking)

name: Large Cash Deposit Followed by Immediate Transfer Out
description: A suspicious transaction pattern where substantial cash is deposited and then immediately transferred out of an account, indicative of money laundering layering techniques. This red flag is exemplified by the Danske Bank case where £200B in suspicious money was allowed to flow through the system.
context: Danske Bank (AML Failure) - Issue: Allowed £200B suspicious money through

name: Unauthorized Account Creation Without Customer Consent
description: Staff creating accounts in customer names without proper authorization or customer knowledge. This misconduct signal was central to the Wells Fargo scandal where employees systematically opened unauthorized accounts to meet sales targets.
context: Wells Fargo (Account Fraud) - Issue: Staff created fake accounts without authorization
Why: Pressure to meet targets; ignored ethics

name: Unauthorized Data Sharing Without Customer Consent
description: Sharing or transferring customer personal data to third parties without explicit customer consent or authorization. This data protection red flag resulted in the Facebook GDPR violation where user data was shared without proper consent mechanisms.
context: Facebook (GDPR Violation) - Issue: Shared user data without consent
Why: Didn't respect user data rights

name: Obligation to Report Suspicious Transactions
description: Staff must identify and report suspicious transactions to compliance authorities. Failure to fulfill this obligation, as demonstrated in the Danske Bank case, results in severe regulatory penalties and reputational damage.
context: Danske Bank (AML Failure) - Why: Staff ignored suspicious transactions
Consequence: €1B fine, CEO resigned, reputation destroyed

name: Obligation to Obtain Customer Authorization for Account Operations
description: Staff must obtain explicit customer authorization before opening accounts or conducting transactions on behalf of customers. Violation of this obligation, as seen in Wells Fargo, constitutes fraud and results in significant fines and criminal prosecution.
context: Wells Fargo (Account Fraud) - Issue: Staff created fake accounts without authorization
Consequence: $3B fine, CEO prosecution, massive layoffs

name: Obligation to Respect User Data Rights and Obtain Consent
description: Organizations must respect customer data rights and obtain explicit consent before sharing or processing personal data. Failure to comply with this obligation, as demonstrated by Facebook's GDPR violation, results in substantial fines and ongoing regulatory investigation.
context: Facebook (GDPR Violation) - Issue: Shared user data without consent

name: Wells Fargo Unauthorized Account Creation Event
description: A major fraud event where Wells Fargo staff systematically created unauthorized accounts without customer knowledge or consent to meet sales targets. This resulted in $3B in fines, CEO prosecution, and massive organizational layoffs.
context: Wells Fargo (Account Fraud) - Issue: Staff created fake accounts without authorization
Consequence: $3B fine, CEO prosecution, massive layoffs

name: Danske Bank AML Screening Failure
description: A critical AML screening failure where Danske Bank allowed approximately £200B in suspicious money to flow through its systems due to staff ignoring suspicious transactions. This resulted in a €1B fine and severe reputational damage.
context: Danske Bank (AML Failure) - Issue: Allowed £200B suspicious money through
Consequence: €1B fine, CEO resigned, reputation destroyed

description: Staff must follow established Standard Operating Procedures and organizational policies including AML, customer identification, and privacy policies. Compliance with documented procedures is mandatory.

description: Staff must report suspicious activity and not ignore potential compliance concerns. This is a critical obligation for AML and fraud prevention.

Keep records of what you did

description: Staff must attend refresher training on an annual basis to maintain current knowledge of compliance requirements, procedures, and regulatory changes.

name: Maintenance of Professional Ethics and Integrity
description: Staff must maintain high standards of professional ethics and personal integrity as a core compliance and conduct obligation. This underpins all other compliance activities.

description: Staff must understand GDPR customer rights and data protection obligations, including data retention periods.

description: Staff must be able to identify and recognize fraud red flags in customer interactions and transactions.

description: Staff must understand when and how to report suspicious activity and other compliance violations.

name: Consequences of Compliance Violations
description: Staff must understand the consequences and penalties associated with violations of AML, KYC, GDPR, and fraud prevention obligations.

name: Account Opening Refusal for Missing Proof of Address
description: Staff must not open an account if a customer cannot provide proof of address; instead, the request must be escalated to a manager.
context: What should you do if a customer can't provide proof of address? A: Don't open account, escalate to manager

name: Tipping-Off Prohibition
description: Staff must not inform a customer that they have matched a sanctions screen, as this constitutes illegal tipping-off under AML regulations.

name: Customer Data Retention Requirement
description: Staff must retain customer data for a minimum of 6 years following account closure, as required by regulatory obligations.

name: Customer Unable to Provide Proof of Address
description: A customer's inability to provide proof of address is a KYC red flag that prevents account opening and requires manager escalation.

name: Direct Debit Guarantee
description: A consumer protection guarantee that provides a full refund of any unauthorized direct debit payment within 10 days of discovery.
